findings.summary: commit_upload_inner calls neither require_writable() nor require_local_io(), and UploadStream records no root, so the commit-time root is caller-chosen: an upload opened on a writable root can be published into a read_only root, and commit with an SFTP root hands the remote POSIX path to the local resolver and hard_link()s into it if that path exists locally. Violates G13/G14 and PRODUCT 18.1/18.2; no unit test and no E4 field covers it.

Budget accounting leaks with no settle path: SendBudget has no session attribution, so messages squeezed out by push_terminal never release the owning session's inflight_bytes (that session is permanently capped), and close_session/sweep_idle drop the session without ever calling budget.settle_file, so the shared 128 KiB budget stays permanently pinned -> node-wide permanent QUEUE_FULL reachable by any token holder (authenticate, read 2 pages, disconnect, repeat). Unit test file_service.rs:2335-2341 freezes the wrong equality as an expectation.

Throttle is fail-open once the bucket table is full: the overflow branch only increments a private global counter and never inserts into `locked`, while authenticate consults is_locked() (which reads only `locked`) and then compares the token anyway. Filling the 1024 buckets is cheap, after which any new principal/source gets unlimited guesses and a correct token still succeeds; THROTTLED is only an error-code label. `global` has no accessor, so probe field throttle_entries_bounded proves memory bounds but cannot see the lost lockout. Contradicts G15/PRODUCT 18.2.

Concurrent session count has no ceiling: authenticate inserts unconditionally; max_sessions and max_browser_sessions appear only inside FileLimits::validate cross-checks and are never used for admission. MODULE.md G16 and PRODUCT 18.2 list 'concurrent sessions' as bounded; idle sweeping bounds lifetime, not count. Each session may open unbounded streams, each with a .part file.

The F2 machine check cannot evaluate true on this tree: send_file_message(s,8) accepts 16 messages (file_drops=1), each 4-byte send_terminal in the 100-loop evicts exactly one whole file message (drain_file_reserve need=4), so the queue is empty after 16 iterations and the later send_terminal(limit) evicts nothing -> squeezed_here=0, so `squeeze_accounting_is_per_message` = (16==16) && (0>1) && (pending==0) = false while the frozen expectation is true. The recorded evidence value final_send_squeezed_messages=15 (.agents/green-evidence...m1.txt:205-206) is unreachable for this code (file_messages_squeezed_out=16 does match). Either the scenario is red or the claimed 9/9 = 77 expectations came from a different tree; must be re-run and corrected honestly.

AuditRecord's #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] is inside the preceding /// doc comment, so the public audit record type silently has no derives; it compiles only because current tests read fields instead of using {:?}/==/clone(). Regression introduced by this batch's G21 refactor; blocks the M2 wire layer from snapshotting audit lines.

list traverses symlinks: is_dir comes from next.metadata() (follows the link, possibly to outside the root) and a single dangling symlink aborts the whole directory page with NOT_FOUND. The adjacent comment claims symlinks are 'never traversed', which is false.

rename's no-overwrite guarantee is check-then-act (dst.exists() then std::fs::rename, which silently replaces on POSIX); unlike commit_upload's atomic hard_link, the race window is neither closed nor declared. G14's 'original bytes untouched' is therefore timing-dependent for another session or local writer.

max_bytes = 0 is accepted and returns an empty page with next_offset == offset and eof = false, breaking G17's monotonic next_offset requirement; validate() only forbids chunk_bytes == 0, not a zero request.

G21 gaps remain: abort_upload (client-reachable, deletes staged bytes), ack_staged and close_session have no recording wrapper, so MODULE.md's 'missing a record is structurally impossible' is false; stage_chunk/authenticate/idle_recycle lines carry root = "", so the five fields G21 promises are not complete for those actions.

Decorative E4 fields: refuses_link only asserts is_err(), so list_rejects_escaping_symlink and write_rejects_escaping_symlink stay true even if resolve's symlink guard is deleted (both then fail for the wrong reason); post_open_reverify_used accepts three codes and is satisfied by resolve alone, so deleting reverify_parent at file_service.rs:1589 keeps it green; locked_after_attempts is a lockout_after+1 constant readback.

capability-negotiation asserts a probe-local decide_channel with no product counterpart (GatewayConfig has no files field; unknown JSON keys are silently dropped), so the scenario's 8 expectations are decoupled from product code - the same 'proves the model, not the product path' defect as r1 F1. The probe header's claim that every field derives from observable engine behaviour is false for this case.

Five of the eight cross-checks MODULE.md claims are individually test-red have no test: chunk_bytes<=max_inflight (179-184), max_ack_bytes<=max_buffered (187-192), the newly added max_ack_bytes>=envelope+entry floor (196-207), max_read_handles>=max_sessions (222-227), and the no-zero rule (150-164). Deleting any of them keeps all tests and scenarios green.

Read-handle quota can never bind: acquire/release are paired inside one synchronous call, so live() is always 0 and peak() always 1; the CAPACITY branch, max_read_handles, the unit assertion peak<=1 and the E4 field peak_read_handles_within_budget are tautologies. G16's 'N chunks of one download cost one handle' currently holds only because reads are synchronous and will need re-wiring in M2.

PRODUCT.md was not updated with this batch: 18.1 still promises the upload ack is 'already persisted bytes' while G18 was corrected to 'staged', still names .nexus-part.* (real name is .<name>.nexus-part-<hex>), and 18.4 still declares the scenarios Red Evidence though they are claimed green.

Only read_page is charged; list pages, stat/mkdir/remove/rename/commit replies and per-chunk acks never touch charge_file, so G16's 'engine charges every outbound file-class message' holds only if a not-yet-existing wire layer volunteers to call send_file_message. send_file_message with an unknown session id also charges the shared budget with no per-session attribution and no release path.

part_creation_refuses_a_preplanted_symlink tests std::fs::OpenOptions directly and never drives open_upload, so changing create_new(true) to create(true) leaves it green; it also early-returns on Windows, the very platform whose PRODUCT 18.3 level-B claim rests on the 'create_new equivalent' premise.

reverify returns FileResult<bool> whose Ok value is always true and never consumed; MODULE.md/PRODUCT.md's 'typed TOCTOU snapshot' has no corresponding type (only a post-operation re-resolve, no pre-op snapshot).
Doc comment references remove_all_in_root, which does not exist (the function is remove_tree at 1712).
A pre-planted symlink/name at the .part path is refused but reported (and audited) as CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE rather than SYMLINK_ESCAPE/EXISTS, so an attack attempt is recorded as a capacity problem.

Two of the three fields cited as F1/F2 evidence (read_page_overflow_code, settle_releases_budget_and_inflight) and several others are emitted but not frozen by any scenario, so regressions there stay invisible; interim_codes is emitted while the 5th-attempt-throttles behaviour it documents is unasserted.
[given] max_inflight_bytes_per_session = 1048576 still describes the pre-r2 default (now 128 KiB); prose-side drift only, no expectation depends on it.

sftp_refusal_gate classifies the refusal by substring-matching the error message; rewording file_service.rs:449-452 flips it to OTHER (fails red, so the direction is safe) - an error-code-level discriminator would be sturdier.

Windows path shape: open accepts an un-prefixed spelling but stores the \?\-prefixed canonical form, so resolve()'s output cannot equal a plain dir.join() - unit test resolve_does_not_truncate_missing_multi_segment_paths would fail on Windows; byte-exact root comparison also rejects case-varied (still canonical) Windows paths, and UNC roots are refused.

close_session takes the source from its caller (sessions never store it), so throttle cleanup only hits if the wire layer passes the right value; SendBudget.terminal_delivered is incremented on acceptance, not actual delivery.
